newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH SEEN HIKING ADVANCES RATE AGAIN - ABN AMRO.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH SEEN HIKING ADVANCES RATE AGAIN - ABN AMRO.

text.p: The Dutch central bank looks set to increase the special advances rate by 30 basis points (bp) to 3.00 percent today, ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said.

The bank said in its Bond Weekly report that the guilder had continued to weaken against the mark despite the advances rate being lifted by 20 basis points two weeks ago to 2.70 percent, 30 basis points below Germany's equivalent, the repo rate.
It said the central bank clearly indicated its unease with the situation by announcing a special advances pact of four days last Thursday, compared with seven days in the previous week.
The pact will have to be renewed on Monday at 1500 GMT.
"We suspect that (the central bank) will close the gap with the German repo in one move, implying a rate increase of 30 bp," ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said.
It said although this may look harsh, the move in the currency had been substantial by Dutch standards.
The mark closed at 1.1262 guilders on Friday, up from 1.1215 in mid-February and 1.1243 just after the first rate hike.
It is nearing its central rate of 1.1267 guilders.
"In addition, given the speed with which the currency has moved, a rate increase of 20 bp would risk an additional hike in the near future," the bank said.
It said that although rates ultimately may have to rise a little above those in Germany, it suspected that bringing them into would be enough.
The special advances rate sets the tone for money market rates.
But the bank did not expect an increase in the secured loans rate, which is comparable to the German discount rate and sets the floor for money rates.
It said a failure to raise this rate may imply the central bank was doing the banking system a favour, but raising it may send out an unattractive and unintended signal.
